text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- The government, at a closed meeting in eastern Austria, said it plans to increase exports by 23 billion schillings by subsidising the industry with an additional 1.3 billion schillings.
- Brickmaker Wienerberger has sold its abrasive materials unit Treibacher Schleifmittel to German industrialist August von Finck.

- The new public limited stock exchange Boerse AG will be dominated by the banks as Bank Austria Chief executive Gerhard Randa will be head of the supervisory board. The reform of Austria's capital market should be over by the end of the year.
- Futures and options trader OeTOB will not be taken over by Kontrollbank because shareholders refused the offer.
- Conservative party leader Wolfgang Schuessel denied the closed meeting of the government was a crisis meeting. A crisis over Bank Austria will not be discussed.
- Austria's pharmaceuticals market growth was up six percent to 17.3 billion schillings. Market leader is Novartis.
- Machinery supplier Auricon expects record orders this year as orders jumped 1.4 billion schillings to 5.9 billion schillings in the first five months.
DIE PRESSE
- Six billion schillings still have to found to fulfil this year's budget expectations, Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger said.
- Austria Tabak's privatisation is due to be started this coming October.

- Industrial group Hutter & Schrantz AG, a subsidiary of Creditanstalt, will lower its dividend to four from five schillings as pre-tax profits dropped to one billion schillings from 6.8 billion schillings.
- A study says Austrian investments are inefficient compared to other EU members.
KURIER
- The government has said Austria will safely meet the Maastricht criteria. A delay of the European Economic and Monetary Union would cost thousands of jobs, it says.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- In order to avoid a budget crisis the government will have to cut 5,000 jobs each year.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Kontrollbank, the government's export financing agency, plans to support exporters with financial guarantees.
- Conservatives want to make the draft telecommunications law more competitive in parliament, even though they accepted it in the council of ministers.
- GiroCredit plans to participate in Macedonian bank Stopanska Banka within the next four weeks.
